You'll notice four things there:
1. The useReducer() call moved from HomePage into JournalProvider.
The provider owns the entries state now. It will survive page navigation because it wraps the router, not just one page.
2. The fetch also lives in the provider.
A useEffect() runs once on mount, fetches all entries, adds a bookmarked flag and a formatted date to each one, then dispatches SET_ENTRIES.
Every page in the app gets entries from context, so no component needs to fetch independently.
3. The context value is { entries, dispatch, isLoading, error, refetch }.
All five are available to any consumer, but each component only takes what it needs:
EntryDetailPage destructures only entries — it has no reason to touch dispatch.
HomePage destructures entries, dispatch, isLoading, error, and refetch, because it handles bookmarking, displays loading and error states, and can trigger a fresh fetch.
4. useJournal() is a custom hook that wraps 'useContext(JournalContext)'.
This is a convenience: consumers import one thing instead of two (useContext() and JournalContext).
Now we need to wire the provider into the app's entry point.
